value.name: Madison Gas and Electric (MGE)
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Madison's residential solar customers this session; MGE is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility. MGE also separately offers a 'Shared Solar' community-solar program, distinct from a customer-owned rooftop system.

permit_authority.value: City of Madison Building Inspection Division (Zoning and Building Inspection)
permit_authority.notes: Wisconsin's Uniform Dwelling Code (UDC) is a genuinely statewide code for one- and two-family dwellings, administered by the state Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS) but enforced locally in every Wisconsin municipality — permit issuance for residential solar in Madison is handled by the City's own Building Inspection Division, not directly by DSPS. Electrical work statewide is separately governed by the Wisconsin Electrical Code (SPS 316, based on the NEC).

interconnection_url.notes: MGE's own page confirms a traditional retail-rate net metering structure (bill credit for excess power delivered to the grid), structurally different from We Energies' buy-back-rate approach elsewhere in Wisconsin (see the utility-comparison note on the We Energies-territory locality researched separately, if published). No specific system-size cap or interconnection fee was stated on the page fetched this session; Wisconsin's statewide interconnection process for utilities is governed by Public Service Commission rule PSC 119.

Properties in a historic district or Planned Development require additional approval steps that may extend the timeline by two weeks or more — this record's same-day figure applies only to the standard, non-complicated path.
